hook_text: A candle, a paraffin stove and a car battery. Millions of South African homes power their evenings this way. Here is why, and how to judge it fairly.
clip_script: Every home needs warmth, light and cooking heat, plus a charged phone. Rural homes often have the grid but cannot afford to cook on it; settlements often have no legal connection. So: wood, free but smoky; paraffin, cheap but poisonous and tippy; candles, cheap and the top cause of shack fires; gas, clean but hundreds of rand up front; solar, safe but cannot cook; grid, everything if you can pay. Homes stack several. Judge each on cost, safety, health, convenience and environment at once, and you will see the cheap ones are the dangerous ones. That is an economics problem as much as a technology one.
visual_style: Whiteboard shack interior with a stove, candle and battery; six option icons appear with ticks and crosses; a comparison matrix fills in with no perfect column.
pacing: Needs, settings, six options, matrix, conclusion.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the comparison matrix for your own household.
